tagline: A valley road reaches a narrowing once guarded in wartime
intro: South of Front Royal, US 340 enters the Page Valley, between the Blue Ridge Mountains and Massanutten Mountain. The highway meets Skyline Drive at Front Royal and crosses tributaries and the railroad on its way through Karo, Limeton and Bentonville to Overall. Near Bentonville, Shenandoah River State Park occupies land along the South Fork. Skyline Caverns, one mile south of Front Royal, offers another view of the valley’s geology below ground, with calcite crystals and connected cave rooms.

At Overall, the road’s earlier identity was the Luray and Front Royal Turnpike. The narrowing valley and the turnpike made Milford, as Overall was then known, strategically important during the Civil War. Confederate troops entrenched south of Milford in September 1864 after retreating up the valley. The highway bridge at Overall dates to 1938, a later structure beside the railway crossing. The battlefield preserves a historic road trace as well as rifle pits and earthworks.

Begin at Front Royal’s Skyline Drive junction and head south, with Skyline Caverns one mile south of town. Continue through Karo and Limeton toward Bentonville and the river park, then reach the county boundary at Overall Run. Here US 340 crosses the run on Overall Bridge beside the railroad, near Milford Battlefield.

moments.title: Skyline Caverns
moments.text: Mud concealed Skyline Caverns’ anthodites until workers cleared a blocked area of the cave. Walter S. Amos discovered the caverns in December 1937 while searching for caves to open in conjunction with Skyline Drive. Mud and clay had to be removed from the floor before the public opening in April 1939. The anthodites are six-sided calcite crystals, protected by Virginia law and kept behind doors opened by a guide. Guided tours reach 260 feet below ground and include stalactites, stalagmites and columns. Three flowing streams are visible along the tour route.

moments.title: Bentonville
moments.text: Bentonville lies on US 340 southwest of Front Royal, near Shenandoah River State Park. The park was established in 1994 and covers 1,619 acres along the South Fork Shenandoah River. Its full name honors Virginia Delegate Andy Guest, a longtime resident of the area. Here the journey’s river landscape has a named public park as well as the highway passing through the village.

moments.title: Overall Bridge
moments.text: Overall Bridge carries US 340 across Overall Run beside the railroad’s bridge, near Milford Battlefield. Built in 1938, it combines a single metal Pratt deck arch truss with four concrete approach spans. The bridge entered the National Register of Historic Places in 2008. The valley narrows at Overall, a feature that made the earlier turnpike strategically important during the Civil War. The battlefield remains privately owned; its recorded features include an earlier turnpike bridge abutment. That older remnant belongs to the turnpike’s history, while the metal truss belongs to the twentieth-century highway crossing.
